Pride, Passion, Success
Welcome
Tony Head Headteacher
My name is Tony Head and I have been the Headteacher of Portswood Primary School since September 2016.
However, I had the pleasure of working at this school over a decade ago and was delighted that I had the opportunity to return as Headteacher.
The support and guidance that comes from working across the MAT is invaluable and I love the feeling of ‘family’ across the partnership. Both the school and I personally have benefited immensely from the depth and breadth of knowledge and support that is available. It has given me the confidence to make informed decisions that I feel are right for the school; ones that have allowed us to continue to strive for excellence for all of our children.
Grosvenor
Shaftesbury
Somerset
Welbeck

Reading
Welcome to our Reading Resource Page!
Here, you'll discover how we foster a love for reading at school and find valuable tips on how you can support your child's reading journey at home. You can learn about our teaching methods and explore practical ways to make reading a fun and enriching experience for your child.
At Portswood, reading lies at the heart of everything we do.
To foster confident, competent and happy readers who actively engage with reading and see it as an important life skill.
This is a key thread that runs throughout our reading curriculum.
Reading is incredibly important for young minds.
It helps children to;
develop their imagination
expand their vocabulary
improve their understanding of the world around them.
Through reading, children explore new ideas, learn about different cultures, and enhance their critical thinking skills. Plus, it's a fun way to discover exciting stories and adventures!
Encouraging a love for reading from an early age sets the foundation for lifelong learning and success
At Portswood, we approach the teaching of reading through four key strands
Early Reading and Phonics
Whole Class Reading (Y2 ownards)
We actively promote and support home reading. We encourage children to read with an adult daily to enhance their reading skills and foster a lifelong love for books.
To celebrate a love of reading we make use of a well-stocked school library and hold special events.

SEND Local Offer
Portswood Primary School recognises its duties under the new SEND Code of Practice which can be viewed here
The Code of Practice is the statutory special educational needs and disability (SEND) system for children and young people aged 0 to 25 from 1 September 2014.
In our school we have access to various specialist services. We have access to services universally provided by Southampton City Council, which are described on the local offer website which can be viewed here.

Sports Premium
This funding is a payment to schools from Central Government and can only be spent on school sport and PE. Schools can choose how best to use the funding to improve and add to the sport and PE provision to help children to develop healthy lifestyles. The funding should be used to build capacity and capability within schools to ensure that improvements made will benefit children joining the schools in future years.
In 2025/26, it is anticipated that Portswood primary will receive £19,000 in funding.

Curriculum
Across Portswood Primary School we provide an enriched, high quality curriculum. Creativity is encouraged; essential skills and knowledge are taught and applied in real life contexts. All children are central to this and viewed as lifelong learners.
The National Curriculum provides exciting opportunities for staff at Portswood to engage and inspire children to be the best they can be; to develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about the world around them and to equip them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, investigate, invent, create and imagine. We believe that developing a mastery of skills, that can be transferable, enables self-confidence and creativity. This in turn helps to foster a sense of pride and achievement.
We develop curious minds by adopting a flexible approach to lesson design and structure. Expert teachers develop expert learners by employing creative teaching methods; developing learning processes; challenging thinking and concepts and developing a ‘can do’ attitude when children are faced with adversity. Teachers are encouraged to think outside of the box, whilst ensuring that skills are understood and applied in a variety of forms. We make use of our own ‘backyard’ to inspire and fascinate children to develop a deeper understanding of the world1.
Together, as staff and children, our curriculum is ever evolving to ensure that we match the needs and interests of our pupils and use the strengths and skills of our staff. Our school curriculum “is not only the subjects on the timetable; it is the whole experience of education”2. Here at Portswood Primary School we provide memorable experiences which in turn provides memorable learning.
Find out more about the curriculum we follow please visit the DfE website (https://www.gov.uk/national-curriculum/overview
2 – Dunford, J, 2012, New head, new school: the challenges and opportunities of starting a school, Nottingham, National College for School Leadership
